1boy, solo, from behind, from below, sword, holding sword, lunging, swinging, foreshortening, faceless

The camera is very close behind the rear shoulder of Character 1 and below waist height. His cloth-wrapped head is turned entirely away, without a visible cheek, eye or facial profile. His broad back occupies the left lower third; his torso twists through a low forward lunge. One bent knee carries his weight while the rear leg extends in the opposing direction. Both hands grip ONE sword at the end of a forceful horizontal sweep across the lower foreground. The near shoulder, wrapped forearms and simple sword hilt establish a readable chain of force; the blade projects diagonally from left toward right with clear perspective. An ivory-white slash arc curves across the middle of the image, like a clean cut opening a heavy charcoal-violet veil. The dark veil is an abstract suggestion of evil spirits: two large torn shadow shapes, not a crowd of monsters with detailed faces. The cut makes a broad quiet pale gap behind the blade, and its shadow edges recoil away from the sword. The warrior looks into the newly opened gap, never back toward the camera. Keep his rough jacket warm muted russet-gray, the shadows black-violet and the backdrop ash-gray with a small dull plum field. Large clean shapes and an asymmetrical opening convey purification, rather than piles of sparkles. One continuous sword blade, connected wrists, a grounded turning body, no weapon floating separately.

masterpiece, best quality, painterly, sketch, visible brush strokes, loose hand-painted texture, broken edges, blocky volume modeling.

A complete illustration with the freshness of a painted sketch, not an unfinished draft. Soft directional light reveals the planes of forms. Build volumes from confident planes of light and shadow with visible brush edges, while letting selected outer contours remain open. Use broad flowing paint masses, dry uneven strokes, and crisp small highlights appropriate to each material. Vary the brush size and edge sharpness between different materials. Preserve deliberate brush marks instead of smoothing every surface.
